items.title: 68099_Erskine Hawkins oral history interview
items.q: Ace Harris was playing piano with me then.

ctx.x: On some of them, a lot of people don't know I did this, "Tennessee Waltz". (laughter) Can you imagine me doing a waltz? Well, I went to do a session with Decca. I was, Avery, not Avery Parrish. Ace Harris was playing piano with me then. At the Savoy barroom, I used to do, late at night, I used to do waltzes cause this was my last hour. It was getting closing time. So, I used to point to different men when they wanted to play a tune. So, they'd just holler. I said give me an E flat, modulate to E flat or a G or…

could sing it in.
So, after we started playing it and
we got it straight, people used to come up there.
Now, this was a medley. People used to come up
and say play that tune that you, about that
Tennessee thing you were talking about. So, they
were talking about the "Tennessee Waltz".
So, I took the tune out and made
a single out of it. And, we just played the
"Tennessee Waltz".
So, I go down to record at Decca.
They said well, what's you gonna do for your
sixth number. I said I'm gonna do "Tennessee
Waltz". They…
